title: ADR-S02: Introduce Kun.Sandbox Module — E2B-compatible sandbox abstraction for Kun consumers
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/adr/kun/ADR-S02-Kun.Sandbox-module.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

本文是原 Kun 的决策记录，引用时写「Kun ADR-S02」。2026-11-18 搬入本仓库时清理了引擎与下游产品的名字：正文照原文，方括号里是整理时替换的说法。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-23
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Related specs:

［智能体引擎的沙箱规格 v1.1］ §2 / §4 / §14 (E2B-compatible surface)

ADR-S01-E2B-compatible-API.md (Supervisor REST API adopts E2B v2 shape)

1. Context

［智能体引擎］ is building a self-hosted Sandbox Supervisor that exposes an
E2B-compatible REST API (see ADR-S01). The Python harness
(［SanYuanAgent］) will drive that Supervisor through an E2B-style
SDK. But sandbox usage is not a Python-only concern: the C# business
services in ［下游的 C# 服务］ have first-class "run this code / run
this command / produce these files" scenarios that today are pushed up
to the Python harness even when the business logic lives in .NET:

Platform: data preprocessing — ingest + transform uploaded CSV/XLSX
into normalised parquet/JSON before handing to analysts.

Edge: document render — run weasyprint / pandoc to convert
reports generated by C# business logic.

Platform: lightweight one-off scripts — tenant-supplied validation
rules or transform functions that must execute in isolation.

Notification: chart render — headless Chromium to turn a
dashboard snapshot into a PNG attached to an email.

These flows currently have three bad options:

Round-trip through the Python harness — the C# service calls the
Python agent service just to borrow a sandbox. Extra hop, extra auth
surface, harness tooling is agent-centric not service-centric.

Each .NET service reinvents a Supervisor HTTP client — drift,
duplicated auth / retry / tracing logic, each service has to learn
the E2B v2 schema from scratch.

Run code directly in the service process — unacceptable: no
isolation, no egress control, no tenant-scoped audit.

The framework layer is the correct place to unify this. Kun already
owns other horizontal infrastructures consumers rely on
(Kun.EventBus, Kun.Storage, Kun.Identity, …); sandbox execution
is the same category: an abstraction with pluggable backends and a
stable surface.

At the same time, ADR-S01 established E2B v2 as the canonical REST
shape for the Supervisor. The .NET abstraction should mirror that
shape exactly so that (a) the code reads the same as the Python SDK,
(b) future migration to E2B Cloud is equally cheap for .NET consumers,
and (c) nothing in Kun.Sandbox becomes a competing abstraction
relative to the Supervisor spec.

2. Problem

Provide a .NET-idiomatic sandbox abstraction that:

Lets any C# service in ［下游的 C# 服务］ (or a future Kun consumer)
create sandboxes, run processes, read/write files, and kill
sandboxes — without knowing whether the backend is a local stub, the
self-hosted Supervisor, or E2B Cloud.

Aligns the interface contract 1-to-1 with the E2B v2 API shape
(endpoints, fields, camelCase JSON), so consumers who already learned
the Python SDK can read .NET call sites unchanged.

Preserves Kun's AOT / zero-reflection posture — callable from
Kun.Gateway, Kun.AspNetCore, or any AOT-strict service.

Does not ship a runtime. The runtime lives in
［SanYuanAgent 的沙箱 Supervisor］ (Python, per Spec v1.1 §14).
Kun.Sandbox is abstraction + client.

3. Decision Drivers

D1 — consumer parity: C# services must have the same sandbox
ergonomics the Python harness already enjoys. Today they don't.

D2 — no drift from the Supervisor spec: every divergence between
the .NET contract and the Supervisor REST contract is a future bug.

D3 — E2B Cloud path preserved: if Mode D (ADR-S01 §14.4) is ever
adopted, .NET consumers should migrate by flipping a registration
line, not by rewriting call sites.

D4 — AOT strict: .NET services in this repo publish AOT.
Sandbox client code must not introduce runtime reflection.

D5 — testability: unit tests for business code that calls a
sandbox must not require Docker; an in-memory provider must exist.

4. Options Considered

Option 1 — No Kun module; each C# service writes its own Supervisor client

Rejected. Directly violates D1 / D2. Guarantees drift. Every
consumer re-learns the E2B schema.

Option 2 — Kun hosts the runtime (port the Python Supervisor into .NET)

Rejected. The Supervisor runtime is deliberately owned by
［SanYuanAgent］ because it manages Docker / gVisor / Envoy /
Browser CDP proxying — all concerns where the Python ecosystem is
stronger and the team's existing ops playbook is already invested.
Re-implementing in .NET gives no consumer value, doubles the operational
surface, and violates Spec v1.1 §14 "Supervisor is Python".

Option 3 — Kun ships a thin abstraction + client, backends are pluggable (✅ selected)

Selected. Kun.Sandbox contains:

Abstractions — ISandboxProvider, ISandboxHandle, IProcesses,
IFiles, and request/response records whose fields mirror the E2B v2
REST shape one-to-one (camelCase at the JSON boundary, .NET-idiomatic
PascalCase in code via JsonPropertyName on records).

Implementations (pluggable):
InMemorySandboxProvider — fake for unit tests; no Docker, no network.

SupervisorSandboxProvider — HTTP client against
/v2/sandboxes/* on the ［智能体引擎］ Supervisor (Phase 1 production path).

E2BCloudSandboxProvider — skeleton that throws NotImplementedException;
to be filled in when Phase 2+ Mode D is actually scoped.


DI — services.AddKunSandbox(opts => opts.UseSupervisor(url, cert) | opts.UseE2BCloud(key, team) | opts.UseInMemory()).

5. Decision

Adopt Option 3. The framework layer gains a new module:

src/Kun.Sandbox/
  Kun.Sandbox.csproj             (IsAotCandidate=true)
  AGENTS.md
  Abstractions/
    ISandboxProvider.cs
    ISandboxHandle.cs
    IProcesses.cs
    IFiles.cs
    SandboxCreateOptions.cs
    ProcessRunOptions.cs
    ProcessResult.cs
    FileEntry.cs
  Implementations/
    InMemorySandboxProvider.cs
    SupervisorSandboxProvider.cs
    E2BCloudSandboxProvider.cs
  Extensions/
    ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
  Internal/
    SandboxJsonContext.cs        (source-generated JSON for AOT)

The interface contract is "the E2B v2 API in C# records":

ISandboxProvider.CreateAsync(SandboxCreateOptions, CT) maps to
POST /v2/sandboxes.

ISandboxHandle.Processes.RunAsync(cmd, ProcessRunOptions, CT) maps
to POST /v2/sandboxes/{id}/processes.

ISandboxHandle.Files.ReadAsync/WriteAsync/ListAsync/DeleteAsync
map to GET/POST/GET .../list/DELETE /v2/sandboxes/{id}/files (with
?path= query parameters per Spec v1.1 §4.5).

ISandboxHandle.KillAsync() maps to
DELETE /v2/sandboxes/{id}.

Record fields carry [JsonPropertyName] attributes that emit
camelCase at the JSON boundary (matching E2B) while keeping
idiomatic PascalCase inside the .NET code. ［智能体引擎］ extensions
(secret scope, browser, egress, max commands) live under a
［智能体引擎扩展属性］ on SandboxCreateOptions serialised as
the ［智能体引擎扩展字段］ sub-object — exactly mirroring the spec.

6. Consequences

Positive

C# business services can directly consume sandboxes through a
typed, AOT-friendly API without learning HTTP / E2B schemas inline.

The abstraction is backend-agnostic: swapping
UseSupervisor → UseE2BCloud is a one-line change when Mode D is
scoped.

Unit tests can use InMemorySandboxProvider with no Docker
dependency.

The interface contract is the E2B v2 shape, so .NET call sites and
Python SDK call sites read the same — lower cognitive load for
engineers crossing stacks.

Negative / Trade-offs

Kun.Sandbox must track E2B v2 API evolution. Mitigation: monitor
E2B changelog (same rule as ADR-S01). Breaking changes cascade
through Kun.Sandbox to all consumers; that is intended.

Kun.Sandbox does not own a runtime. Any expectation that a
local UseInMemory() provides real isolation is wrong — it is a test
fake. AGENTS.md and XML docs are explicit about this.

The Supervisor client path requires S2S JWT + mTLS to the Supervisor.
Callers must wire Kun.Security (or an equivalent S2S token source)
into the HttpClient via a DelegatingHandler. Docs show the
canonical wiring.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
Consumer drifts the record shape away from E2B schema	CI contract test: SandboxCreateOptions / ProcessResult JSON output diffed against a golden fixture derived from E2B v2 docs; diff > 0 fails the build.
InMemorySandboxProvider leaks into production wiring	AddKunSandbox + UseInMemory name signals "test only"; AGENTS.md calls it out; follow-up can add a KUN_SANDBOX_ALLOW_INMEMORY_IN_PROD=false guard if abuse appears.
Supervisor upgrades a field shape mid-flight	Records use [JsonPropertyName] + JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull so additive changes are backward-compatible; breaking changes require an explicit version bump.
E2B Cloud provider is tempting to "finish early"	The stub throws NotImplementedException with a clear message. Filling it requires a dedicated task after Mode D is scoped — not a drive-by.

7. Alternatives not taken

Owning the runtime in .NET (Option 2): rejected; Supervisor is Python
by design.

A single provider that branches internally on BackendKind: rejected;
three explicit implementations are clearer and each can carry its own
dependencies / tests.

Exposing raw HttpClient with helper methods: rejected; would force
every consumer to re-derive the URL shape and undermine the
abstraction's reason for existing.

8. Validation

Spec alignment: SandboxCreateOptions JSON payload (camelCase,
cpuCount/memoryMB/timeoutMs/envs/metadata/［智能体引擎扩展字段及其子字段］)
matches the request body in Spec v1.1 §4.3 byte-for-byte.

AOT: CI AOT-publish matrix adds Kun.Sandbox and runs
dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror with zero warnings.

Tests: tests/Kun.Sandbox.Tests/ includes ≥ 15 tests (in-memory
lifecycle, Supervisor request-shape via WireMock.Net, E2B-Cloud stub
surface, DI options round-trip, camelCase serialisation, parallel
sandbox isolation).

9. References

ADR-S01-E2B-compatible-API.md (parent, Supervisor REST shape)

［智能体引擎的沙箱规格 v1.1］ §§1.3, 2, 4, 12, 14, 17

ADR-009-Kun.Configuration-module.md (sibling example of an
Abstraction-layer module with pluggable backends)

E2B Cloud API docs — tracked external
contract this module mirrors

toc.text: Option 1 — No Kun module; each C# service writes its own Supervisor client
Option 2 — Kun hosts the *runtime* (port the Python Supervisor into .NET)
Option 3 — Kun ships a thin abstraction + client, backends are pluggable (✅ selected)

title: When to use ICurrentUser vs IAuthenticatedUser
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/design/when-to-use-currentuser.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

The host selects the authentication scheme and registers a request-scoped adapter. Choose the interface by the data and authentication context the caller needs.

Interface	Data available to the caller	Runtime source
Kun.Core.Security.ICurrentUser	UserId, PrincipalKind, Roles, IsAuthenticated	Kun.Security.Security.JwtCurrentUser after S2S validation, or a host's browser or platform adapter
Kun.Identity.IAuthenticatedUser	Core fields plus an optional ClaimsPrincipal, tenant id, email and display name	Kun.Identity.AspNetCore.KunCurrentUser in an OIDC cookie host
Kun.Identity.Abstractions.ICurrentUser	Core fields plus an optional Kun.Security.Principal snapshot	Identity.Client reads the authenticated session or validated service identity
Kun.Identity.Abstractions.IAuthenticatedUser	Guaranteed Principal and UserId	A platform contract for callers that have already required authentication. The default client registers the nullable current-user view

AddKunIdentityAspNetCore registers the core and browser interfaces against the same scoped adapter. AddKunIdentityClient makes the platform current-user interface available and offers its implementation to core callers through a scoped alias. The core alias uses TryAddScoped, so an explicitly registered core adapter retains its place. Background workers can supply AnonymousCurrentUser.Instance.

Decision table

Caller scenario	Inject	Why
gRPC service handler (S2S JWT)	ICurrentUser	The validated S2S principal supplies subject, kind and roles.
gRPC interceptor / pipeline behaviour	ICurrentUser	Same — operates at the S2S boundary.
ASP.NET Core API endpoint the browser hits directly	IAuthenticatedUser	Cookie middleware populated TenantId / Email / Name / Principal; skip the cast.
ASP.NET Core background worker (BackgroundService)	ICurrentUser with a null check	No request scope exists; bind AnonymousCurrentUser explicitly.
Outbox publisher	ICurrentUser, usually AnonymousCurrentUser.	Background context — obtain any required identity from the authenticated message context. OpenTelemetry baggage carries diagnostic context.
Unit test	ICurrentUser with a hand-rolled fake (a record MyUser(…) : ICurrentUser) or AnonymousCurrentUser.Instance.	Tests depend only on the narrow interface; no HTTP context is needed.
Component that reads tenant (EF filter, cache key)	ITenantContext, not either of these.	Tenant identity propagation has its own abstraction — don't couple persistence-layer code to an auth interface.

How to extend correctly

Happens rarely. When you need a new field:

Is it present on S2S JWT claims? → add to ICurrentUser and
to every implementation. Update
docs/adr/kun/ADR-008-Kun.Identity-module.md with the
rationale.

Is it browser / cookie only? → add to IAuthenticatedUser.
Update docs/adr/kun/ADR-010-Kun.Identity-cookie-session.md.

Is it a concern of a different subsystem? (tracing, tenancy,
feature flags) → add it to the subsystem's own abstraction
(ITenantContext, ITracedCurrentUser, …) and have the
current-user binding expose or forward it there if needed.
Example precedent: ITracedCurrentUser carries TraceId without
polluting ICurrentUser.

Anti-patterns (do not do these)

❌ ICurrentUserEx / IEnhancedCurrentUser / ICurrentUserV2 —
every one of these reinvents IAuthenticatedUser. If
IAuthenticatedUser is missing a field, add the field to
IAuthenticatedUser after reading Kun ADR-010, don't fork.

❌ A per-service ICurrentUser subinterface in
a downstream consumer — consumer
services get no value from owning the abstraction.

❌ ClaimsPrincipal injection as a first-class service —
always go through IAuthenticatedUser.Principal. Direct
ClaimsPrincipal injection hides which host provided it.

❌ Mutable ICurrentUser implementations — instances are
scoped to a single request; mutating one breaks baggage
assumptions for the async context.

❌ Making ICurrentUser depend on
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext — Kun.Core is BCL-only
and the interface stays there so non-HTTP hosts (gRPC-only
workers, integration tests) can target it without ASP.NET Core
in their closure.

If you think you need something new

Read this doc end-to-end. Yes, including the anti-patterns.

Read Kun ADR-008 and Kun ADR-010.

Post the proposed field + its source (JWT claim / cookie /
header / derived) in the PR description and call out which
interface it belongs to per the decision rules above.

If none of the rules fit, write an ADR that supersedes / extends
Kun ADR-010 with the new concern — before adding code.

If the addition is still ambiguous after all that, leave the code
as-is and raise it at the next framework review. The cost of one
extra sprint of "injecting IAuthenticatedUser and casting to
something" is far lower than the cost of shipping a third
sibling abstraction that every downstream service then has to
track.

授权主体类型

PrincipalKind 是 principal_kind 的只读身份投影。内置 JWT / Cookie 适配器与 HTTP/gRPC 权限入口使用同一个主身份读取规则，Mediator 从 ICurrentUser 取值。不能从调用请求的 JSON、头或角色名推断它。旧自定义适配器默认 user；如果适配器代表服务或 Agent，必须显式实现此属性，不能让机器身份继续使用用户默认值。

端口登记与次序

ICurrentUser 与 ITenantContext 只由身份 / 多租户适配器登记：AddKunSecurity()（JwtCurrentUser）、AddKunIdentityAspNetCore()（KunCurrentUser）、AddKunMultiTenancy()，或宿主自己的适配器。数据与审计组件不占这两个端口：AddKunDataConventions<TContext>() 与 AddKunAuditing<TContext>() 的拦截器在上下文创建时按需解析，没有登记时按匿名（AnonymousCurrentUser）、无租户（NullTenantContext）记录。所以适配器在数据组件之前或之后登记都生效，不存在「先登记数据组件就把身份适配器挤掉」的次序约束。

AddKunSecurity()、AddKunIdentityAspNetCore() 以 TryAdd 登记：同一宿主装了多个真实适配器时先登记者生效，要换实现就显式 Replace；AddKunMultiTenancy() 也以 TryAdd 登记租户上下文，保留宿主选择的实现。

宿主自己的服务构造注入 ICurrentUser、而宿主又没有身份适配器时（后台作业、迁移任务），显式登记 AnonymousCurrentUser.Instance；框架不再顺带替它登记。

KunDbContext 的构造需要 ITenantContext：单租户宿主显式登记 NullTenantContext.Instance。

title: Why Kun Splits Writes from Reads
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/design/why-cqrs.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

Kun enforces a hard boundary between the write side and the read side of every bounded context.
This is not a stylistic preference — it is enforced by module dependencies and verified by CI.
Understanding the reasoning helps you work within the model rather than against it.

The write side: consistency first

Command handlers use KunDbContext directly or inject a repository port defined by their domain. The write side loads an aggregate, calls domain methods,
and delegates to IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync. That single call does several things atomically:

Applies EF Core change tracking to produce the correct SQL.

Collects domain events from every modified IAggregateRoot via ChangeTracker.

Dispatches domain events to in-process handlers via IDomainEventDispatcher.

Converts any resulting integration events into OutboxMessage rows.

Commits the aggregate changes and the Outbox rows in one database transaction.

This sequence exists because consistency is the write side's job. A command either fully
succeeds — business state updated, domain events dispatched, integration events enqueued — or
it fully fails with no observable side-effects. The Specification pattern keeps query logic out of
handler code while still letting the repository translate rich criteria into SQL without leaking
EF Core types up into the domain layer.

The cost is performance. Loading aggregates, tracking changes, and running the full pipeline
takes more work per request than a raw SQL insert. For the write side this is the correct
trade-off: correctness matters more than throughput.

The read side: performance first

Query handlers open connections from a dedicated read-side NpgsqlDataSource (potentially
pointing at a read replica) and run raw SQL with Dapper; Kun does not wrap either library. No EF
Core context is involved; there is no change tracker, no aggregate loading, no domain logic.

The result is flat DTOs returned directly to the caller. Because there is no object graph to
navigate and no invariants to enforce, the read side can denormalize freely: a single query can
join five tables and return a DTO shaped exactly for the API response, avoiding the N+1 problems
that appear when EF Core navigation properties are misused.

The read side can also be published as a native AOT binary, which the EF Core write side cannot.
Dapper's classic Query<T> builds its row readers with reflection, so an AOT-published service
adds Dapper's source generator (Dapper.AOT, [DapperAot]) or reads rows with
NpgsqlDataReader directly; see read-side patterns.

How the Command/Query divide maps to Kun.Mediator

KunMediator dispatches every IRequest<TResponse> to its registered handler through a
FrozenDictionary<Type, RequestHandlerBase> — O(1) lookup with zero runtime reflection. Handlers
are registered explicitly at startup via KunMediatorBuilder. The mediator does not scan
assemblies; there is no runtime discovery.

Pipeline behaviors wrap each dispatch. The standard write-side stack is:

ValidationPipelineBehavior   ← rejects invalid commands before touching the database
UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior   ← calls SaveChangesAsync after the handler returns
LoggingBehavior              ← structured log at entry and exit
TracingBehavior              ← opens an OpenTelemetry span per dispatch

Query handlers carry only LoggingBehavior and TracingBehavior by default — there is nothing
to validate or commit. Adding UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior to a query handler is a configuration
mistake that the type system cannot prevent, but CI code review does. The distinction is
explicit: every registration in Program.cs names the request type, the response type, and the
handler type. There is no magic.

Trade-offs to be aware of

Two models to maintain. Every write-side aggregate and its corresponding read-side DTO are
separate representations. When you add a field to an aggregate you must also update any queries
and DTOs that need to surface it. The consistency guarantee you get from the write side does not
automatically flow to the read side.

Denormalization can drift. Read-side DTOs are shaped for API consumers, not normalized from
aggregate state. If a consumer's requirements change and the DTO is updated but the underlying
data is not re-projected, the read side and the write side can express different views of the
same entity.

No EF Core in query handlers. Using EF Core in a query handler breaks the UoW pipeline
behavior's transaction boundary assumptions and gives up the option of publishing the read side
as a native AOT binary. Neither the compiler nor the project references enforce this — command
and query handlers usually live in the same project — so reviewers check that query handlers
take no EF Core types.

The split is explicit and by design. It makes each side independently optimizable and keeps the
invariants of each clearly scoped.

title: Why Kun Uses the Outbox Pattern
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/design/why-outbox.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

When a service saves a business entity and publishes an integration event, those are two separate
I/O operations. The Outbox pattern exists to make them behave as one. This document explains the
problem, Kun's solution, and the trade-offs you accept.

The dual-write problem

Consider the naive approach to event publishing:

await dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();          // (1) aggregate persisted
await broker.PublishAsync(integrationEvent); // (2) event published to RabbitMQ

These two operations are not atomic. Any failure between (1) and (2) leaves the system
inconsistent: the database reflects the new state but consumers never learn about it. Retrying
(1) is unsafe — it may double-write. Putting (2) before (1) has the mirror problem: the event
fires but the database write fails.

Worse, the broker itself is a network dependency. A transient RabbitMQ outage at step (2) means
lost events with no recovery path — unless you build one yourself. That recovery logic is exactly
what the Outbox pattern provides.

How Kun atomizes the publish

Kun's write-side pipeline centers on EfUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync. The sequence inside that
method is:

Domain events are collected from ChangeTracker.Entries<IAggregateRoot>() and dispatched
in-process via IDomainEventDispatcher.

Each domain event handler calls IIntegrationEventBus.Publish inside an
EventEnvelopeScope. The writer resolves the stable type identifier and the registered
source-generated JSON metadata, then serializes the payload inside a v1 envelope.

The writer captures the origin, tenant and trace context and stages the complete
OutboxMessage in the request's IntegrationEventBuffer.

The unit of work attaches the staged rows to the same context and calls
DbContext.SaveChangesAsync. Aggregate changes and Outbox rows commit in one transaction.

How the background publisher drains the Outbox

Hosts call AddKunOutboxRelay<TContext>() for regular Kun contexts or AddKunOutboxRelay()
for registered strict contexts. The relay claims pending PostgreSQL rows with a committed
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lease, restores each row’s stored trace parent and publishes the
envelope. Each broker confirmation updates that row immediately. The Order sample uses a
logging publisher. Production hosts can register the RabbitMQ publisher with AddKunEventsBroker.

Transient failures persist the attempt count and next attempt time. Invalid envelopes and rows
that reach the retry limit move to Failed. On shutdown the relay finishes its current row and
returns unissued rows. If the process exits, another replica can claim them after lease expiry.

Consumer idempotency via IProcessedMessageStore

Because the publisher uses at-least-once delivery — the broker acknowledgement and the database
MarkPublished update are still two operations — a consumer may receive the same message more
than once. Before dispatch, the subscriber checks IProcessedMessageStore for this consumer
and event ID. It writes the success mark after the handler completes, then acknowledges the message.

The Redis key is idemp:{consumerName}:{messageId}. The default retention is seven days.
A failure between the business commit and the success mark can cause another delivery.
Handlers that write business data should use the message ID as an idempotency key within
their own transaction.

Trade-offs to be aware of

Latency is measured in seconds, not milliseconds. The background publisher runs on a polling
interval. A consumer will see an event seconds after the originating transaction commits, not
sub-millisecond. If your design requires synchronous cross-service consistency, the Outbox is not
the right tool — gRPC calls with Result-based error handling are.

The Outbox store requires a reliable database. The pattern works because the database is the
source of truth for pending messages. If the database is unavailable, no messages are published —
but this is safer than losing messages silently. Recovery is automatic once the database is
reachable again.

Failed messages need a recovery workflow. Messages that exhaust retries end up in the
Failed state. There is no automatic dead-letter re-queue for failed Outbox messages; you need
an operational process to inspect, correct, and republish them.

The Outbox pattern adds operational surface area in exchange for a guarantee that the dual-write
problem cannot silently corrupt your system state. That trade is almost always worth making in a
distributed system where correctness matters.

See also

Kun ADR-015 Outbox pattern design — full design walk-through: type
surface, atomicity boundary, publisher pump, consumer idempotency, rejected alternatives.

AGENTS.md §运行时约定 (the Outbox rule) — normative rules (atomicity,
stable event IDs, idempotent consumers); how the W3C trace context crosses the outbox is shown in the
tracing tour. The rules constrain; this primer explains the problem; the
ADR explains the design.

title: Getting Started with Kun Framework
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/getting-started.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

This tutorial takes about 10 minutes. By the end you will have the full sample stack running
locally, have sent an order through the Order service's command flow, and have a mental model of
how the pieces fit together.

Prerequisites

Requirement	Version	Notes
.NET SDK	10.0.404	Verified with the roll-forward policy in global.json
Docker Desktop	Any recent stable	Runs PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Redis containers
curl and jq	curl 7.82+	Send JSON requests and read the returned IDs
Visual Studio Build Tools (Windows only)	Optional	Required only for AOT native publish

Verify your SDK version:

dotnet --version
# the walkthrough was tested with 10.0.404

Verify Docker is running:

docker info
# must succeed — no "Cannot connect" errors

Clone and build

git clone https://github.com/CavaiLAB/kun.git
cd kun
dotnet restore Kun.slnx
dotnet build Kun.slnx -c Release --no-restore

Run the framework unit suite using the solution filter from CI:

dotnet test --solution tests/kun-unit.slnf -c Release --no-build

Run the samples

The AppHost starts the services and their infrastructure. Trust the ASP.NET Core localhost
development certificate so Order can call Catalog over HTTPS. Create a private directory outside
the repository for the local issuer's keys and Order's short-lived service token:

dotnet dev-certs https --trust
umask 077
export SampleCredentials=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'SampleCredentials=%s\n' "$SampleCredentials"
dotnet run --file samples/local/catalog-credentials.cs -- "$SampleCredentials"
dotnet run --project samples/Kun.Sample.AppHost

Aspire prints a dashboard URL to the console, typically:

Login to the dashboard at: http://localhost:15888

Open that URL in a browser. You will see the Aspire Dashboard with:

Panel	What it shows
Resources	Live health of catalog, order, gateway, postgres, rabbitmq, redis
Logs	Structured log streams per service, filterable by level
Traces	Distributed OpenTelemetry traces across all service boundaries
Metrics	Request rates, latency histograms, CPU and memory

Wait for Catalog and Order to finish applying their EF Core migrations before sending requests.

Find the service ports

Copy the HTTP URLs for catalog and order from the Endpoints column in Resources.
Set these variables to the two URLs shown in your dashboard:

CATALOG=http://localhost:54242
ORDER=http://localhost:54243

Place an order

Run these requests in a second terminal. Set SampleCredentials to the path printed during
startup. The local token lasts five minutes. To renew it, run
dotnet run --file samples/local/catalog-credentials.cs -- "$SampleCredentials" with the same
directory as the first terminal. Order reads the updated token on its next HTTPS call.

Create a Catalog product with stock, then order two units using its returned identifier:

PRODUCT_ID=$(curl -fsS "$CATALOG/products" --json '{
  "name":"Demo notebook","description":"Grid paper","price":12.50,
  "categoryId":"f4743227-31ea-4312-b9ca-e7183786bb01","initialStock":5
}' | jq -er .)
ORDER_ID=$(curl -fsS "$ORDER/demo/orders" --json "{
  \"productId\":\"$PRODUCT_ID\",\"quantity\":2,\"unitPrice\":12.50
}" | jq -er .orderId)
curl -fsS "$ORDER/demo/orders/$ORDER_ID" | jq '{id,status,totalAmount}'

The order reads back as Completed with a total of 25.00. The handler reserved two units over
gRPC and committed the order and its order.completed.v1 envelope in one transaction. To see
the event, open the Order resource's console logs and look for the Outbox publisher's
Would publish event 'order.completed.v1' message. In this sample the publisher logs delivery.

Without a request body, POST /demo/orders tries two random product IDs. Catalog rejects the
reservation. Order returns 422 BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATED and writes no order or Outbox row.

Open Traces in the Aspire Dashboard and filter by order. You will see the HTTP request, the
Mediator.Send PlaceOrderCommand span, and the gRPC call to Catalog under the same trace. After the
walkthrough, stop the AppHost and remove the temporary credentials directory.

What you just saw

The order flow exercised these building blocks:

Outbox transactional publishing — the order row and its integration event were written in a
single EF Core SaveChangesAsync call. If the database transaction rolled back,
no message was produced. The KunOutboxRelay drains Pending rows to the
configured publisher asynchronously. The sample publisher logs each event.

W3C Trace Context propagation — every OutboxMessage row stores the traceparent and
tracestate headers captured at enqueue time. The background publisher resumes the trace when it
publishes. The request and the corresponding Outbox publish span share a TraceId in the
Aspire Dashboard Traces panel.

Next steps

Simpler CQRS story — samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/ demonstrates DDD aggregates, write/read
split with EF Core and Dapper, and Outbox event publishing. Its
README walks through the file structure.

Architecture essays — understand the design trade-offs:
Why CQRS?

Why Outbox?


Module map — docs/design/module-map.md shows the
full dependency graph and which modules are AOT candidates.

Root AGENTS.md, section Kun 框架的构建、测试与代码约定 — the binding
architectural rules that every code contribution must satisfy, including the four-layer dependency
constraint and AOT restrictions.

title: Gateway 限流策略指南
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/guides/gateway-rate-limit.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

Kun.Gateway.RateLimiting 把 ASP.NET Core 内置的 RateLimiter 包装成策略 × 分区的两维组合：
三种分区解析（partition resolver）× 三种限流策略（limiter policy）= 九种可选配置，计数在进程内。限流一共有三套入口，对照见下一节。
参考：docs/design/why-cqrs.md · 白皮书 §12.2

三套入口

限流有三套入口，都登记在 ASP.NET Core 的限流中间件上，超出额度时返回 429。

入口	包	计数放在哪里	多副本之间
AddKunRateLimit	Kun.RateLimit	进程内，固定窗口	不共享，每个进程各自计数
AddKunRateLimiter、AddKunSlidingWindowRateLimiter、AddKunTokenBucketRateLimiter	Kun.Gateway	进程内，固定窗口、滑动窗口或令牌桶	不共享，每个进程各自计数
网关代理路由的限流	Kun.Gateway	Redis，固定窗口	连同一个 Redis、网关配置相同时共用额度

AddKunRateLimit（Kun.RateLimit）

登记：services.AddKunRateLimit(o => o.AddWindow("api", w => { w.PermitLimit = 100; w.Period = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1); }))，命名空间 Kun.RateLimit.Extensions。每个窗口登记为一个同名的策略，端点写 RequireRateLimiting("api")。

计数：用 System.Threading.RateLimiting 的固定窗口限流器，在进程内计数。

分区：每个窗口按 WindowRule.PartitionKey 分区，取 Tenant（默认）、User 或 Ip。

超限：返回 429 和 Retry-After，再调用 KunRateLimitOptions.OnRejected（设置了的话）。

用在：宿主自己的端点，一次登记几个命名窗口，各自设额度、窗口长度与分区键。

AddKunRateLimiter 一组（Kun.Gateway）

登记：命名空间 Kun.Gateway.RateLimiting。AddKunRateLimiter() 登记 kun-default（固定窗口，每分钟 100 次），AddKunSlidingWindowRateLimiter() 登记 kun-sliding-window，AddKunTokenBucketRateLimiter() 登记 kun-token-bucket；端点写 RequireRateLimiting(策略名)。

计数：用 System.Threading.RateLimiting 的固定窗口、滑动窗口或令牌桶限流器，在进程内计数。

分区：由 IRateLimitPartitionResolver 决定，宿主没有登记时按租户，见「分区解析」。

用在：宿主自己的端点，算法可选固定窗口、滑动窗口或令牌桶。AddKunGateway() 总会调用 AddKunRateLimiter()，并给没写 RateLimiterPolicy 的 YARP 路由补上 kun-default，见「网关默认边界」。

网关代理路由的限流（Kun.Gateway）

登记：没有单独的扩展方法。AddKunGateway(configuration, …) 传入带路由与集群的 GatewayConfiguration 时启用，MapKunGateway() 把它绑到全部代理端点。每条路由必须写 RateLimiterPolicy，取 kun-default、tenant 或 user，否则装配时拒绝。

计数：在 Redis 里计数，用 Kun.RateLimit 的 IRedisRateLimitStore（固定窗口）；宿主要登记 IConnectionMultiplexer。

多副本：副本连同一个 Redis，且键前缀、Issuer 与路由配置相同时，共用额度。

分区与额度：kun-default 按可信客户端 IP；tenant 按租户，user 按租户内主体，匿名或身份不完整时都按 IP。额度、窗口与键前缀取 Gateway:RateLimits，见「声明式网关路由」。

用在：声明式配置路由的网关（如组件网关），代理路由的额度在多个副本之间共用。

分区解析 (IRateLimitPartitionResolver)

决定"同一个限流桶由谁共享"。从 HttpContext 里取一个字符串 key。

实现	分区依据	适用
IpRateLimitPartitionResolver	HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress	匿名 API、防 abuse
TenantRateLimitPartitionResolver	已验证外部 JWT 的 tenant_id claim	多租户共享库场景（默认）
UserPrincipalRateLimitPartitionResolver	已验证外部 JWT 的 sub claim	Free-tier API，per-account 限额

注册：任意一种用 services.AddSingleton<IRateLimitPartitionResolver, XxxResolver>()。Kun 的 AddKunXxxRateLimiter() 系列扩展会用 TryAddSingleton<...,TenantRateLimitPartitionResolver>() 做默认，你预先注册就覆盖它。

限流策略 (IRateLimiterPolicy)

决定"桶里怎么发放许可"。

策略	行为	特点	默认值
FixedWindow（AddKunRateLimiter）	每 N 秒重置计数	最简单、内存最低，边界突刺	100 permits / 1 min
SlidingWindow（AddKunSlidingWindowRateLimiter）	分段滑动	平滑，无突刺；内存与 SegmentsPerWindow 线性	100 / 1 min / 6 segments
TokenBucket（AddKunTokenBucketRateLimiter）	令牌累积 + 匀速补充	吸收突发流量；适合 webhook fanout、批量导入	100 tokens burst，20 / 10s 补充

三者均调用 AddRateLimiter() 注册一个具名策略："kun-default"、"kun-sliding-window"、"kun-token-bucket"。端点开启时写：

app.MapGet("/orders", handler).RequireRateLimiting(KunRateLimiterExtensions.SlidingWindowPolicyName);

网关默认边界

AddKunGateway() 已注册 kun-default，并为未显式设置 RateLimiterPolicy 的 YARP 路由绑定它。业务路由同时默认要求认证；只有配置 AuthorizationPolicy: "Anonymous" 的路由可匿名访问。普通 ASP.NET 端点仍需调用上面的 RequireRateLimiting。三种内置策略超限均返回 429；限流器提供重试时间时，响应附整数秒 Retry-After。具名自定义策略也沿用默认拒绝回调，除非宿主显式覆盖。

IP 分区仅读取 Connection.RemoteIpAddress。宿主须在认证和限流之前调用 UseForwardedHeaders()；独立网关已接好。Gateway:TrustedProxyAddresses（IP 列表）和 Gateway:TrustedProxyNetworks（CIDR 列表）只填写实际反向代理出口，ForwardLimit 默认 1。两张名单均为空时关闭转发头处理，非信任来源伪造 X-Forwarded-For 不会切换限流桶。不要单独清空框架的 KnownProxies/KnownIPNetworks：框架会将其理解为信任全部。

典型组合

1. 多租户 SaaS，边界精度要求一般

builder.Services.AddKunRateLimiter();   // Tenant partition + FixedWindow

2. 按用户限流，平滑曲线

builder.Services.AddSingleton<IRateLimitPartitionResolver, UserPrincipalRateLimitPartitionResolver>();
builder.Services.AddKunSlidingWindowRateLimiter(o => { o.PermitLimit = 60; o.Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1); });

3. 防 DDoS 按 IP，允许突发

builder.Services.AddSingleton<IRateLimitPartitionResolver, IpRateLimitPartitionResolver>();
builder.Services.AddKunTokenBucketRateLimiter(o =>
{
    o.TokenLimit = 500;
    o.TokensPerPeriod = 50;
    o.ReplenishmentPeriod = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);   // 50 req/s 稳态
});

Redis 后端：跨 Pod 分布式计数

内置的 FixedWindow / SlidingWindow / TokenBucket 策略都是进程内（每个 Gateway pod 各自独立计数）。在多 pod 部署时 100 permits 会变成 100 × podCount 的实际吞吐。

Kun.RateLimit.IRedisRateLimitStore 提供基础 primitive：

using Kun.RateLimit.Extensions;

services.AddSingleton<IConnectionMultiplexer>(ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect("redis:6379"));
services.AddKunRedisRateLimitStore(o => o.KeyPrefix = "kun:prod:rl");

调用：

var result = await store.HitAsync("tenant-a", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));
// result.Count 现在有多少个命中、result.ResetsIn 距离重置还有多久
if (result.Count > 100) { /* reject */ }

Redis 用一条 Lua 脚本完成计数、查询剩余 TTL 和设置有效期。首次命中与已有计数但缺 TTL 的桶会得到完整窗口。正常后续命中沿用已有到期时间。服务侧与网关可以共用这个存储实现。

声明式网关路由

在 Gateway:Routes 中为每条路由指定 RateLimiterPolicy。组件网关把 kun-default 映射到可信客户端 IP、tenant 映射到租户、user 映射到租户内主体。网关使用 Gateway:RateLimits 中的前缀、窗口和各分区额度。所有副本配置相同的 Redis 连接与前缀即可共享额度。额度用尽时返回 429 和 Retry-After，存储不可用时返回 503。

title: NuGet 包迁移指南
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/guides/package-migration.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

首个合并版发布后，从平台 0.x 或内核 2026.10.25 升级的项目可按以下步骤选择版本。内核档从 nuget.org 还原，平台档从 CavaiLAB 的 GitHub Packages 还原。beta 版本的两档包均从 GitHub Packages 还原。

在该版本的 GitHub Release 下载 NuGet.config 与 release-packages.json。前者列出准确的包源映射，后者列出该版本的全部包和档位。已有包源配置的项目合并相应条目。

使用有读取包权限的账号与令牌设置 KUN_PLATFORM_FEED_USER 和 KUN_PLATFORM_FEED_TOKEN，然后更新项目的 PackageReference。采用中央包管理的项目还需更新 Directory.Packages.props。

将使用的 Kun 包固定到同一个日历版本。使用内部接口的包之间声明精确版本依赖。运行 dotnet restore --configfile NuGet.config，再构建并执行项目的测试。

平台 0.x 的包

以下对照覆盖 GitHub Packages 上已发布的 54 个包。这些包从 0.3.0 起停更，已发布的所有版本均保留，固定版本的项目可以继续还原。一行有多个目标时，可按使用的功能选取。

已发布包	合并版包	引用说明
Qian.Audit	Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore	EF 与命令审计。
Qian.Audit.Abstractions	Kun.Audit.Abstractions	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Audit.Native	Kun.Audit.Postgres	原生 PostgreSQL 审计。
Qian.Authz	Kun.Authorization.Rbac	RBAC 权限计算。
Qian.Authz.Abstractions	Kun.Authorization.Rbac.Abstractions、Kun.Authorization	RBAC 契约与内核授权端口按使用方引用。
Qian.Authz.AspNetCore	Kun.Authorization.AspNetCore	HTTP 与 gRPC 的授权入口。
Qian.Capabilities	Kun.Capabilities	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Capabilities.Abstractions	Kun.Capabilities.Abstractions	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Capabilities.AspNetCore	Kun.Capabilities.AspNetCore	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Config.Abstractions	Kun.Configuration.Abstractions	配置契约进入内核档。
Qian.Config.Apollo	Kun.Configuration.Apollo、Kun.Configuration.Platform	前者接 Apollo 配置源，后者提供组件登记、开关与平台配置管理。

Qian.Data	Kun.Data、Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL	平台装配使用前者，自定义 EF 宿主按需引入 PostgreSQL 租户迁移生成器。
Qian.Data.Abstractions	Kun.Data.Abstractions、Kun.EntityFrameworkCore	数据服务契约在前者，严格上下文与 EF 数据会话契约在后者。
Qian.Data.AspNetCore	Kun.Data.AspNetCore	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Data.Dialect.Pg	Kun.Data.Dialect.Pg	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。

Qian.Files	Kun.Files、Kun.Storage.Local	文件服务使用前者，本地传输与签名实现使用后者。

Qian.Tenancy	Kun.Tenancy、Kun.MultiTenancy	租户开通使用前者，基础租户作用域与消息传播使用后者。
Qian.Tenancy.Abstractions	Kun.Tenancy.Abstractions	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。
Qian.Tenancy.AspNetCore	Kun.Tenancy.AspNetCore	更新包引用与对应的命名空间。

内核包的替代项

停发的包	使用方要做的调整
Kun.Audit	命令审计契约使用 Kun.Audit.Abstractions，按宿主选择 Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore 或 Kun.Audit.Postgres。
Kun.Auditing	实体变更审计迁至 Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore。
Kun.Dapper	原生 PostgreSQL 通道使用 Kun.Data.Native.Postgres 与 Kun.Data.Native.Abstractions。逐条迁移自定义 SQL。
Kun.Infrastructure	写侧直接使用业务 DbContext 与工作单元，读侧直接投影为查询 DTO。
Kun.MultiTenancy.EntityFrameworkCore	引用 Kun.EntityFrameworkCore，更新注册扩展所在的命名空间。
Kun.Saga	补偿编排器归档。依赖它的业务需要保留当前版本，或在应用中迁移编排与补偿逻辑后升级。
Kun.Sandbox	沙箱已归档。先迁移宿主中的隔离实现，再移除包引用。
Kun.Storage	引用 Kun.Storage.Abstractions，并按后端选择 Kun.Storage.Local、Kun.Storage.S3 或 Kun.Storage.Oss。

同名包的行为变化

Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ 使用组件事件信封与相应拓扑。升级前核对发布端与订阅端的交换机、路由键、消息形状和消费者组，协调切换生产与消费。

Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore 属于平台档，升级时将这个包的源映射指向 GitHub Packages。实体审计与业务事务的接线见该版本的包说明。

Kun.AspNetCore 与 Kun.Grpc 不再自带权限判定。HTTP 端点的 RequireKunPermission 与 gRPC 的授权拦截器（AddKunAuthorizationInterceptor）由 Kun.Authorization.AspNetCore 提供，它属于平台档，从 GitHub Packages 还原。原来用这两处权限判定的项目要引用它，只从 nuget.org 还原的项目要为它映射源。没有登记授权拦截器时，Kun.Grpc 拒绝执行标了 [RequiresPermission] 的方法。

Kun.Gateway 提供类库。把宿主的可执行入口切到网关宿主，使用平台外壳时再引用 Kun.Gateway.Shell。选项类型 KunGatewayOptions 换成 Kun.Gateway.Abstractions 里的 GatewayConfiguration，ExternalIssuer、ExternalAudience、InternalIssuer 依次改名为 IdentityIssuer、IdentityAudience、Issuer。Redis 固定窗口计数器的类型（IRedisRateLimitStore、RateLimitHitResult、RedisRateLimitStoreOptions、RedisFixedWindowRateLimitStore）改在 Kun.RateLimit 命名空间，注册扩展 AddKunRedisRateLimitStore 改在 Kun.RateLimit.Extensions。

租户上下文使用 Guid? 表示租户或平台作用域。处理消息与网络输入时先验证租户标识，数据库与既有消息的文本按原有格式读写。

Kun.MultiTenancy 不再提供可替换的租户解析器与选项：DefaultTenantResolver、ITenantResolver、ITenantIdSource、KunMultiTenancyOptions 与 AddKunMultiTenancy(Action<KunMultiTenancyOptions>) 已删除。宿主登记 AddKunMultiTenancy()，在认证之后挂载 UseKunMultiTenancy()。租户只从已认证主身份唯一的 tenant_id 读取，请求头不再作为来源，没有缺省租户回落。

Kun.Security 的 AddKunSecurity() 不再登记 ITenantContext，JwtTenantContext 已删除。需要租户上下文的宿主另调 AddKunMultiTenancy()。

IKunPlugin<TConfig> 的实现通过 ConfigTypeInfo 提供源生成的 JSON 元数据。使用 JsonSerializerDefaults.Web 保持配置属性名匹配规则。

HTTP 错误与进程内错误使用 Kun.Errors 定义的错误码和 ErrorDetail。依赖旧错误字面或响应结构的调用方需要同步更新解析逻辑。

各项公共 API、注册方法与部署变更见版本变更记录。

title: Read-Side Patterns: Writing Query Handlers
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/guides/read-side-patterns.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

This guide covers the recommended patterns for query handlers in Kun. It assumes you understand
the write/read split; for the reasoning behind that split see
docs/design/why-cqrs.md.

The Write/Read Rule

Query handlers must not use KunDbContext, IUnitOfWork, or any EF Core type. They open a
connection from an NpgsqlDataSource, run raw SQL with Dapper, and return flat DTOs. Kun does not
ship a read-side package: the application references Npgsql and Dapper directly. The rule is not
enforced by the build, so reviewers check that query handlers take no EF Core types.

The short version:

Command handler: inject IRepository<T> or KunDbContext (via EF). Transactional.

Query handler: inject NpgsqlDataSource. No change tracking, no aggregates.

Recommended Query Handler Pattern

The standard shape for a Kun query handler:

using Dapper;
using Kun.Core.Cqrs;
using Npgsql;

public sealed class GetProductByIdQueryHandler(NpgsqlDataSource readDataSource)
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductByIdQuery, ProductDto?>
{
    public async ValueTask<ProductDto?> Handle(
        GetProductByIdQuery request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await using var connection = await readDataSource.OpenConnectionAsync(cancellationToken);

        const string sql = """
            SELECT "Id",
                   "Name",
                   "Description",
                   "Price",
                   "CategoryId",
                   "Stock"
            FROM   "catalog"."catalog_products"
            WHERE  "Id" = @Id
              AND  "IsDeleted" = false
            """;

        return await connection.QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<ProductDto>(
            new CommandDefinition(sql, new { request.Id }, cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
    }
}

This is the handler from
samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/GetProductByIdQueryHandler.cs.

Key points:

NpgsqlDataSource.OpenConnectionAsync returns an open connection from the data source's
pool. Dispose it with await using; disposing returns it to the pool.

Parameterized SQL via the anonymous object new { request.Id }. Never interpolate values
directly into the SQL string.

Pass the cancellation token through CommandDefinition, so a cancelled request also cancels
the query.

Column names match the DTO property names exactly (case-sensitive on PostgreSQL). The
catalog's EF mapping keeps PascalCase column names, so the query selects them quoted; with
snake_case columns, alias each one with AS "PropertyName".

Schema-qualify table names. The catalog tables live in the catalog schema, and the read
connection does not set search_path.

Soft-delete filter ("IsDeleted" = false) applied directly in SQL. There is no EF Core
global filter on the read side — the SQL is the filter.

The handler returns null when no row matches; the endpoint turns that into Results.NotFound(),
and Kun.Errors.AspNetCore (UseKunErrors()) writes the empty 404 as an ErrorDetail with the
error code NOT_FOUND.

Registering the Read-Side Data Source

Register one NpgsqlDataSource for the read side in Program.cs:

var readCs = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("CatalogDbRead") ?? writeCs;

builder.Services.AddSingleton(_ => NpgsqlDataSource.Create(readCs));

The container owns the data source and disposes it on shutdown.

Give the read side its own connection string to point it at a replica; the catalog sample
falls back to the write connection when ConnectionStrings:CatalogDbRead is not set.

If the application talks to more than one PostgreSQL database, register each data source under
a key (AddKeyedSingleton) and resolve it with [FromKeyedServices], so a handler cannot pick
up the wrong one.

Pagination

Kun does not ship paging types. Define the request and result shapes your API needs next to the
query:

public sealed record ListProductsQuery(int Page = 1, int PageSize = 20) : IQuery<ProductPage>;

public sealed record ProductSummaryDto(Guid Id, string Name, decimal Price, int Stock);

public sealed record ProductPage(IReadOnlyList<ProductSummaryDto> Items, int TotalCount);

Run the count and the page on the same connection. Dapper's QueryMultiple does both in one
round trip:

public sealed class ListProductsQueryHandler(NpgsqlDataSource readDataSource)
    : IRequestHandler<ListProductsQuery, ProductPage>
{
    public async ValueTask<ProductPage> Handle(
        ListProductsQuery request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await using var connection = await readDataSource.OpenConnectionAsync(cancellationToken);

        const string sql = """
            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "catalog"."catalog_products" WHERE "IsDeleted" = false;
            SELECT "Id", "Name", "Price", "Stock"
            FROM   "catalog"."catalog_products"
            WHERE  "IsDeleted" = false
            ORDER  BY "Name", "Id"
            LIMIT  @PageSize OFFSET @Offset;
            """;

        var parameters = new { request.PageSize, Offset = (request.Page - 1) * request.PageSize };
        await using var multi = await connection.QueryMultipleAsync(
            new CommandDefinition(sql, parameters, cancellationToken: cancellationToken));

        var totalCount = await multi.ReadFirstAsync<int>();
        var items = (await multi.ReadAsync<ProductSummaryDto>()).ToArray();
        return new ProductPage(items, totalCount);
    }
}

Page is 1-based; validate Page and PageSize in the query's validator.

Order by a unique key last ("Id" above), so rows do not move between pages.

For large tables, prefer keyset pagination (WHERE ("Name", "Id") > (@AfterName, @AfterId))
over OFFSET, which reads and discards every skipped row.

DTO Design

DTOs on the read side are intentionally flat. They are shaped for the API consumer, not for the
domain model.

Rules:

No aggregate nesting. A ProductDto does not contain an OrderDto. If a view needs data
from two aggregates, join the tables in SQL.

No domain types. DTOs use primitive types (string, decimal, Guid, int) or simple
value types. Never expose Money, Address, or other value objects from the domain layer in a
DTO — that would create a dependency on Kun.Core in the read result.

Name for the consumer, not the table. Column aliases can differ from table column names.
Shape the DTO for what the API consumer needs to display or act on.

Immutable records. Use sealed record with positional properties for DTOs. Records are
value-comparable, serializable, and clearly signal "data container, not entity".

The ProductDto from the catalog sample:

// samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/ProductDto.cs
public sealed record ProductDto(
    Guid Id,
    string Name,
    string Description,
    decimal Price,
    Guid CategoryId,
    int Stock);

The query from GetProductByIdQuery:

// samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/GetProductByIdQuery.cs
public sealed record GetProductByIdQuery(Guid Id) : IQuery<ProductDto?>;

IQuery<TResponse> is a marker interface in Kun.Core.Cqrs that extends IRequest<TResponse>.
Using IQuery rather than IRequest directly signals intent and allows pipeline behaviors to
discriminate between commands and queries at registration time.

Anti-Patterns

Do not inject KunDbContext in a query handler

// Wrong — do not do this
public sealed class GetProductByIdQueryHandler(CatalogDbContext db)
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductByIdQuery, ProductDto?>
{
    public async ValueTask<ProductDto?> Handle(...)
    {
        return await db.Products
            .Where(p => p.Id == request.Id)
            .Select(p => new ProductDto(...))
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken);
    }
}

Problems with this pattern:

CatalogDbContext inherits KunDbContext which has global query filters, change tracking, and
concurrency checks active. A query handler does not need any of this and pays the overhead.

Kun.EntityFrameworkCore is not AOT-compatible (no IsAotCompatible in its csproj). Injecting it into a
query handler that runs in an AOT-published service will fail at publish time with trim warnings
or at runtime with reflection errors.

UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior calls SaveChangesAsync after every registered handler in the
write pipeline. If a query handler is registered in the same pipeline stack as a command
handler that has UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior, the query will trigger a SaveChangesAsync
call. This is harmless but wasteful — and it signals a pipeline configuration mistake.

Do not load aggregates and project at runtime

// Wrong — loads the entire aggregate graph, then discards most of it
var product = await _repository.GetByIdAsync(request.Id, ct);
return new ProductDto(product.Id, product.Name, ...);

Problems:

Loading an aggregate through IRepository<T> uses EF Core change tracking. Every property on
the entity is loaded even if the DTO only needs three of them.

If the aggregate has navigation properties (owned entities, collections), EF Core may issue
additional queries. The N+1 problem manifests here.

The aggregate is loaded into memory, partially read, then immediately discarded. The CPU and
allocation cost is wasted.

Kills AOT compatibility for the same reasons as injecting KunDbContext directly.

Write the SQL to return only the columns you need. If the SQL feels verbose, that verbosity is
honest — it reflects exactly what data is fetched.

AOT Note

Dapper's classic API (QueryAsync<T>, QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<T>) builds the row reader for
T with runtime reflection, so it is not trim- or AOT-safe. Kun does not wrap Dapper. If a
service that runs query handlers is published with Native AOT, choose one of these in that
service's own project:

add Dapper's source generator (the Dapper.AOT package) and mark the query methods with
[DapperAot], so the reader is generated at build time; or

read rows with NpgsqlDataReader directly and construct the DTOs by hand.

Either way, dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true with warnings as errors catches a reflection-based
read path before deployment. The catalog sample is not AOT-published and uses the classic API.

title: Schema-per-service with KunDbContext
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/guides/schema-per-service.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

Scope: how to run multiple Kun-based services against a single PostgreSQL
instance by giving each service its own schema (catalog, order, …), with
business tables, the Outbox, and the EF migrations-history table
all co-located under that schema.
Applies to: any KunDbContext-derived DbContext using Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.
Last updated: 2026-04-22.

Why schema-per-service

Running many services against one physical Postgres instance is operationally
cheap (one cluster to patch, one backup path, one connection pool). But putting
everything in public makes name collisions inevitable — two services both want
an outbox_messages, an __ef_migrations_history, and so on.

Kun's answer: each service overrides KunDbContext.DefaultSchema with its own
name ("catalog", "order", etc.), and UseKunSchema(schema) on the options
builder wires the migrations-history table into the same schema. A
SchemaConsistencyInterceptor then fails fast at the first SaveChangesAsync
if the two ever disagree, so misconfigurations surface in dev instead of
silently leaking rows across schemas in production.

End-to-end recipe

1. Override DefaultSchema on your DbContext

using Kun.Core.MultiTenancy;
using Kun.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

public sealed class CatalogDbContext : KunDbContext
{
    public DbSet<Product> Products => Set<Product>();

    public CatalogDbContext(
        DbContextOptions<CatalogDbContext> options,
        ITenantContext tenantContext)
        : base(options, tenantContext)
    {
    }

    /// <inheritdoc/>
    protected override string? DefaultSchema => "catalog";

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder); // applies HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)
        modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new ProductConfiguration());
    }
}

KunDbContext.OnModelCreating calls modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)
before applying the Outbox and tenant-filter configurations, so every
unqualified .ToTable("x") lands under catalog.

2. Chain UseKunSchema("catalog") in the design-time factory and DI

The design-time factory drives dotnet ef migrations add:

using Kun.Core.MultiTenancy;
using Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.Extensions; // UseKunSchema lives here
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design;

internal sealed class CatalogDesignTimeFactory
    : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<CatalogDbContext>
{
    public CatalogDbContext CreateDbContext(string[] args)
    {
        var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<CatalogDbContext>()
            .UseNpgsql("Host=localhost;Database=catalog_design;Username=postgres;Password=postgres")
            .UseKunSchema("catalog")   // wires MigrationsHistoryTableSchema
            .Options;

        return new CatalogDbContext(options, NullTenantContext.Instance);
    }
}

Same pattern in the runtime AddDbContext call:

services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((_, options) =>
    options
        .UseNpgsql(connectionString)
        .UseKunSchema("catalog"));

Order matters: .UseNpgsql(...) must precede .UseKunSchema(...) so the
relational provider extension already exists by the time UseKunSchema mutates
MigrationsHistoryTableSchema.

3. Regenerate migrations under the new schema

For an existing service already carrying public-schema migrations, regenerate
them once:

# Remove the old public-schema migrations
dotnet ef migrations remove \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --force

# Re-add under the new schema — the DesignTimeFactory's UseKunSchema("catalog")
# drives the correct MigrationsHistoryTable schema.
dotnet ef migrations add Initial_SchemaQualified \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations

Inspect the generated _Initial_SchemaQualified.cs — every CreateTable /
CreateIndex / DropTable call now carries schema: "catalog", and the
generated ModelSnapshot.cs starts with .HasDefaultSchema("catalog").

Windows / Git Bash note

Both of the commands above must run with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 in Git Bash,
otherwise --project values get path-mangled:

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 dotnet ef migrations add Initial_SchemaQualified \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations

Run the two services' dotnet ef migrations add commands sequentially
(not in parallel) — they compete for the same src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore
build artefacts.

4. Create the schemas in Postgres

dotnet ef database update will call EnsureSchema("catalog") via the
generated migration, so in most cases you do nothing. For a plain
EnsureCreatedAsync() flow (tests / quick prototyping), EF also issues
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS catalog. You can create the schemas ahead of
time if you want the service accounts to have restricted grants:

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS catalog;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "order";  -- note: 'order' is reserved, quote it
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA catalog TO svc_catalog;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA "order" TO svc_order;

5. Verify with dotnet ef migrations list

After migrations regenerate, confirm the history table lives in the right
schema:

dotnet ef migrations list --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog
# shows catalog.__ef_migrations_history
dotnet ef migrations list --project samples/Kun.Sample.Order
# shows order.__ef_migrations_history

The safety net: SchemaConsistencyInterceptor

KunDbContext.OnConfiguring unconditionally registers a
SchemaConsistencyInterceptor whose job is exactly one thing: compare
Model.GetDefaultSchema() against the relational provider's
MigrationsHistoryTableSchema at the first SaveChangesAsync, and throw
InvalidOperationException with a remediation hint when they diverge.

This catches the most common error — overriding DefaultSchema on your
DbContext but forgetting to call UseKunSchema(...) on the options builder.
Without the interceptor, business tables would land under catalog while
__ef_migrations_history silently stays in public, a migration-drift
timebomb. With the interceptor, the first save fails loudly:

InvalidOperationException: KunDbContext.DefaultSchema='catalog' does not match
MigrationsHistoryTable schema='(null)'. Call .UseKunSchema("catalog") on
DbContextOptionsBuilder to wire both consistently.

The check is gated by Interlocked.CompareExchange so it runs exactly once
per DbContext instance — zero overhead after the first transaction.

Outbox co-location

Because the KunDbContext base class applies HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)
before ApplyConfiguration(new OutboxMessageConfiguration()), the Outbox
table inherits the same schema without any extra configuration.

This is deliberate — having catalog.outbox_messages in the same schema as
catalog.catalog_products lets a single transaction atomically commit both,
which is the entire point of the Outbox pattern. Putting the outbox in a
shared outbox schema would break that atomicity story (cross-schema writes
still commit atomically, but the operational mental model gets muddier, and
separate grants / backup policies become harder to reason about).

Running multiple services against one PostgreSQL

Once each service has its own schema, they can target the same physical
Postgres instance and the same logical database. Aspire wires this up
trivially — the Kun.Sample.AppHost sample points Catalog and Order at
the same postgres resource:

var postgres = builder.AddPostgres("postgres");
var kun = postgres.AddDatabase("kun");

builder.AddProject<Projects.Kun_Sample_Catalog>("catalog")
    .WithReference(kun);
builder.AddProject<Projects.Kun_Sample_Order>("order")
    .WithReference(kun);

With schema-per-service in place, the two services coexist without name
collisions — each SELECT * FROM catalog.outbox_messages stays well-scoped.

Reference implementation

src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/KunDbContext.cs — DefaultSchema virtual
property + auto-registration of the interceptor.

src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Extensions/KunDbContextOptionsBuilderExtensions.cs —
the UseKunSchema extension.

src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Interceptors/SchemaConsistencyInterceptor.cs —
the fail-fast guard.

samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Infrastructure/CatalogDbContext.cs + migrations —
concrete example with a catalog schema.

samples/Kun.Sample.Order/Infrastructure/OrderDbContext.cs + migrations —
concrete example with an order schema.

tests/Kun.IntegrationTests/Persistence/SchemaPerServiceTests.cs —
Testcontainers-backed test that boots two KunDbContext subclasses under
distinct schemas against one Postgres and asserts physical isolation in
information_schema.tables.

title: Tracing Tour: Reading Distributed Traces in the Aspire Dashboard
content:
本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/guides/tracing-tour.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

This document walks through the OpenTelemetry traces you will see when running the Kun sample
stack via dotnet run --project samples/Kun.Sample.AppHost. It assumes Docker and the Aspire
workload are installed and the stack is running. For setup instructions see
docs/getting-started.md.

W3C Trace Context and OTLP

Every Kun service propagates traces using the
W3C Trace Context standard. Each in-process span records
a traceparent header that carries the TraceId and SpanId. When a request crosses a process
boundary — HTTP, gRPC, or the Outbox — the receiving side extracts the parent context and creates
a child span under the same TraceId. The result is a single trace tree that spans every hop
from the initial HTTP request to the final consumer acknowledgement.

Spans are exported via OTLP. When running under .NET Aspire the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
environment variable is set automatically to the Aspire Dashboard's collector endpoint. The
Dashboard collects and renders all spans without any additional configuration in the services
themselves. Framework modules (src/Kun.*) contain no OTel package dependencies — all
AddKunObservability wiring lives in the sample composition root
(samples/Kun.Sample.Shared/OpenTelemetryExtensions.cs) so the framework remains AOT-clean.

What Instruments What

Kun.Mediator

ActivitySource name: Kun.Mediator

TracingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> wraps every ISender.Send and IPublisher.Publish call
(see src/Kun.Mediator/Behaviors/TracingBehavior.cs). It starts an ActivityKind.Internal span
named Mediator.Send {RequestTypeName} — for example Mediator.Send CreateProductCommand or
Mediator.Send GetProductByIdQuery.

The span is a child of the ambient activity at dispatch time, which is typically the ASP.NET Core
server span for the incoming HTTP request. Because the Mediator span is internal, it appears as a
nested block directly under the HTTP span in the Dashboard timeline.

Tags set on this span:

Tag	Value
(none beyond span name)	The request type name is encoded in the span name

If you want to add custom tags (e.g. command ID, tenant ID), do so from within the handler by
calling Activity.Current?.SetTag(...).

Kun.EventBus.EntityFrameworkCore

ActivitySource name: Kun.EventBus.EntityFrameworkCore

The EF relay creates one ActivityKind.Producer span named outbox.publish for each delivery
attempt. The envelope writer stores the W3C parent identifier and trace state with the Outbox
row during the command. The relay restores that parent before handing the stored envelope to
the configured publisher. A retry creates another span with the same message ID.

Tags set on outbox.publish:

Tag	Value
messaging.system	outbox
messaging.destination	Stable event type ID, e.g. product.published.v1
messaging.message_id	UUID of the OutboxMessage row

Kun.Grpc

ActivitySource name: Kun.Grpc

KunTracingInterceptor (see src/Kun.Grpc/Interceptors/KunTracingInterceptor.cs) runs first in
the interceptor chain registered by AddKunGrpc. It starts an ActivityKind.Server span named
grpc.server for each unary, client-streaming, server-streaming or duplex RPC call. The span
remains active until the awaited handler completes, including all stream operations.

Tags set:

Tag	Value
rpc.system	grpc
rpc.method	Full gRPC method path, e.g. /catalog.CatalogService/GetProduct
rpc.type	unary, client_streaming, server_streaming or duplex_streaming
rpc.grpc.status_code	Final gRPC status code; faults also mark the activity as Error

If a downstream service calls a Kun gRPC service, the caller's HttpClient instruments propagate
the traceparent header via the standard gRPC client instrumentation wired in
AddKunObservability. The server interceptor picks up the parent context automatically from the
incoming metadata — ActivityKind.Server causes the OTel SDK to look for an inbound W3C header.

How to Read a Happy-Path Trace

Place an order using the Catalog and Order endpoints in the getting started walkthrough.
Find its POST /demo/orders request in the Aspire Dashboard.

The mediator span contains the gRPC stock reservation for each order line.

The handler stages an order.completed.v1 envelope in the same transaction as the order.
The envelope carries the producer, actor, message ID and W3C trace parent.

The EF relay claims the row and opens outbox.publish with its stored parent. The Order
sample logs the delivery. Its span tags include the event type and message ID.

In a host configured with RabbitMQ, the publisher sends the envelope to qian.events
under the subject order.completed. A registered subscriber restores the envelope's parent
for its consume order.completed span and acknowledges after successful processing.
The publish and consume spans share the trace that the command stored in the envelope.

How to Read Outbox Lag

Outbox lag is the time between when an integration event was enqueued (the producer's
SaveChangesAsync commit) and when it was actually published to the broker (the
outbox.publish span).

To measure lag in the Dashboard:

Find the Mediator.Send span for a command that produces an integration event (e.g.
CreateProductCommand).

Note its end timestamp — this is approximately when SaveChangesAsync committed and the
outbox row was written.

Find the outbox.publish span for the same message (match by messaging.message_id, or by
messaging.destination + approximate time).

The start timestamp of outbox.publish minus the end timestamp of the producer span is
the outbox lag for that message.

The EF relay immediately polls again after a nonempty batch. The following defaults apply to
KunEventsOptions in the publisher host.

Setting	Default	Effect
BatchSize	100	Maximum rows claimed per context per cycle
PollInterval	1 second	Delay after an empty cycle
PublishTimeout	10 seconds	Confirmation deadline per message
LeaseDuration	30 seconds	Other replicas can claim unfinished rows after expiry
MaxAttempts	5	Maximum attempts after transient failures
RetryBaseDelay	1 second	Initial exponential backoff

A message in OutboxStatus.Failed will not be retried automatically. Monitor for Failed rows
in the outbox_messages table and alert on them — they represent messages that could not be
delivered after all attempts.

Pitfalls and Common Gaps

Background services that do not start an activity

KunOutboxRelay is a BackgroundService implementation.
Its ExecuteAsync loop does not have an ambient Activity unless one is explicitly started.
This means:

Any log message emitted inside the loop but outside a span will have no TraceId attached in
structured logs.

Any child activity started without an explicit parent context appears as a root span in OTLP.

If you add custom background services to your application and want their spans connected to
a broader trace, you must restore the parent context manually — the same pattern used by
KunOutboxRelay with ActivityContext.TryParse.

async void timers and fire-and-forget

Avoid async void methods and _ = Task.Run(...) inside handlers or background services.
Exceptions thrown on async void paths crash the process without ending any open spans, leaving
dangling incomplete spans in the Dashboard. Use async Task and await throughout.

Gateway observability

The standalone Kun.Gateway host registers AddKunObservability with service name
kun-gateway, configured through KunObservability. EF instrumentation is disabled because
this host does not access EF. Native AOT hosts must set IncludeEfCore=false; a runtime-feature
guard removes that reflection-based path at link time and rejects attempts to enable it at runtime. ASP.NET request spans cover proxy and JWKS requests, while
HttpClient instrumentation covers downstream calls; there is no separate custom transform span.
The gateway remains in the Native AOT audit. Consumers that reference the gateway package in
their own host choose their own observability registration.

Key span names to recognize at a glance

Span name	Source	Meaning
Mediator.Send {Type}	Kun.Mediator	A command or query was dispatched
outbox.publish	Kun.EventBus.EntityFrameworkCore	An outbox row was published to the broker
consume {subject}	Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ	The subscriber dispatched an envelope
grpc.server	Kun.Grpc	A unary or streaming gRPC call was handled

本页由本仓库的发布标签生成，源文件为 docs/design/module-map.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。 Version：0.1.0-phase1（2026-04-23 发布）。该版本建立了初始矩阵。持久化与租户模块按当前源码更新。 任何下游仓库对 Kun.* 的消费都应以本表为 SoT（Single Source of Truth）。 Phase 1 模块矩阵 图例：AOT 状态 ✅=项目文件写了 IsAotCompatible=true（普通构建就开着裁剪、AOT 与单文件分析器；CI 的 AOT 冒烟宿主 tests/Kun.AotSmoke 整体扎根原生发布，ILC 零警告）；⚠️=trim-safe 但非 AOT（见历史文档 AOT 审计（2026-04-23））。 Core 层 模块 职责 典型用途 主要 API AOT 测试 Kun.Core 领域抽象（AggregateRoot / ValueObject / DomainEvent / Result / Error）、ITenantContext、ICurrentUser、ISystemClock 所有 Kun.* 的编译期零依赖基底；下游服务的 DDD 建模直接使用这些类型 AggregateRoot / Result / Error / ITenantContext ✅ 34 分发与校验（Abstraction 层） 模块 职责 典型用途 主要 API AOT 测试 Kun.Mediator FrozenDictionary 无反射 CQRS 调度器 + Pipeline Behaviors 所有业务 Command/Query 的执行入口 AddKunMediator(builder => …) / ISender / IPublisher ✅ 8 Kun.Validation IValidator + ValidationPipelineBehavior 命令入口的统一校验 AddValidator() ✅ 12 Kun.Configuration 强类型 Options + DataAnnotations + fail-fast 下游服务的配置装配 AddKunOptions() ✅ 13 平台端口增量（2026-10-09） 模块 职责 主要 API AOT Kun.Authorization 权限判定、进程内数据过滤表达式与字段策略端口，无权限引擎 IPermissionChecker、IDataPermissionFilter、IFieldPolicy true，CI 验证 Kun.Configuration.Apollo HTTP 配置源、长轮询、签名和缓存 AddApollo、ApolloOptions true，CI 验证 Mediator、ASP.NET Core 和 gRPC 增加对 Authorization 的依赖；具体语义与迁移见 Kun ADR-016。历史 Phase 1 表保留为原始版本快照。 错误模型合一（S1-KUN-023） 模块 职责 主要 API AOT Kun.Errors 错误码与错误码目录、Error、ErrorException、RFC 9457 problem+json 的 ErrorDetail；零依赖 ErrorCode、ErrorCatalog、Error、ErrorException、PlatformErrors true，CI 验证 Kun.Errors.AspNetCore HTTP 错误映射：ErrorException 与框架自己产生的错误一律写成 ErrorDetail AddKunErrors、UseKunErrors、KunResults.Error true，CI 验证 Kun.Core 的 Error、ErrorType、ResultFailureException 与 DomainException 删除，Result 失败时带 Kun.Errors 的 Error；Kun.Validation 的 ValidationError、ValidationException 删除，校验失败给 INPUT_INVALID 与逐项字段错误（字段级错误码 + JSON Pointer）；Kun.AspNetCore 只做端点映射（MapCommand、MapQuery），AddKunAspNetCore、异常处理器与 ToProblemDetails 删除；Kun.Grpc 按错误码的 HTTP 状态映射 gRPC 状态码。上面 Phase 1 表里这几行按原样保留。 中介登记可叠加（S1-KUN-023） AddKunMediator 可以对同一个服务集合调多次：第一次建 KunMediatorBuilder 并登记 KunMediator、ISender、IPublisher，之后的调用往同一个 builder 里加，几个模块各自登记的处理器与行为合进同一个中介。同一请求只能有一个处理器，登记第二个时当场抛 InvalidOperationException。AddPermissionBehavior 多一个带 PermissionBehaviorOptions 的重载，只改这一个请求取权限判定器与当前主体的方式，判定算法与拒绝映射不变。描述符被拷进另一个服务集合时，那个集合另建自己的 builder，不往原来的 builder 里加。权限行为因装配不全（没有判定器、没有权限声明）拒绝时记一条警告日志，与正常的无权分得出来。 组件运行时（S1-KUN-023） 模块 职责 主要 API AOT Kun.Runtime 组件运行时：插件装载、服务键与注入、类型化事件、可逆副作用、扁平 scope；只引用 Kun.Errors PluginLoader、IPluginContext、IKunPlugin、KunEvent、ScopeKey — 运行时不带产品语义：ScopeKey 只查语法（global，或小写的种类名加非空 id），种类有哪些由平台档定；声明式表面的目录键 SurfaceKeys 在平台档。语言无关的场景用例在 tck/runtime，.NET 一侧是 tests/Kun.Runtime.Tests。 插件开发包（S1-KUN-023） 模块 职责 主要 API AOT Kun.Plugin.Sdk 内核档契约：组件的代码声明、生成契约与清单错误、命令策略协议 KunPluginAttribute、CapabilityAttribute、CommandPolicies、CommandInvocation — Kun.Plugin.Sdk.Commands 平台档契约：能力命令管道（权限、事务、数据会话、主体端口检查）与钩子能力 AddKunCapability、CommandDataSession、ExposeCapabilityHook — Kun.Plugin.Sdk.Generators 源生成器与 KUNSDK001–003 诊断，只以分析器引用 — — Kun.Plugin.Sdk.AspNetCore 平台档契约：HTTP 插件可见性 AddKunPluginEndpoints、UseKunPluginEndpoints、RequireKunPlugin — 清单工具在仓库根的 tools/Kun.Plugin.Tool，不打包。Kun.Plugin.Sdk 不依赖平台档的包：CommandInvocation 带的 Principal 在内核契约 Kun.Security.Abstractions 里。 持久化（Infrastructure 层） 模块 职责 典型用途 主要 API AOT 测试 Kun.EntityFrameworkCore 写侧 EF Core 实现 + KunDbContext + Outbox 落库 + 多租户过滤器 所有业务写路径；事务边界与 Outbox 同事务 AddKunEntityFrameworkCore() / KunDbContext ⚠️ trim-safe 53 Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL EF 迁移的 PostgreSQL 租户 RLS 生成器 在租户表上生成行级策略 UseKunTenantRlsMigrations() — — Kun.Data.Abstractions 平台数据与方言契约 数据类型、序号、迁移与连接目录 IDataDialect / IDataMigrator — 27 Kun.Data 平台的 EF 数据组件 在组件中打开强约束数据会话 AddKunData() — 39 Kun.Data.AspNetCore 数据目录 HTTP 端点 公布基准类型与连接档案 MapKunData() — 15 Kun.Data.Dialect.Pg PostgreSQL 方言 登记基准类型映射与连通性探测 AddKunPgDialect() — — Kun.Data.Native.Abstractions 原生数据会话和事务的契约 通过插件上下文使用原生数据服务 INativeDataService / INativeDataSession ✅ — Kun.Data.Native.Postgres 原生数据会话的 PostgreSQL 实现 访问受租户范围约束的数据库连接 NativeDataComponent ✅ 17 写侧使用业务数据上下文，读侧可直接使用 Npgsql 数据源与 Dapper。读侧模式 事件与编排 模块 职责 典型用途 主要 API AOT 测试 Kun.EventBus.Abstractions 稳定事件标记、注册与查询端口 只声明事件的契约包 IEventTypeRegistrar / IIntegrationEvent ✅ 3 Kun.EventBus 集成事件 / Outbox 抽象 + 后台发布器 + 消费端幂等 跨服务发布/消费 *.IntegrationEvent AddKunEventBus(eb => eb.Register("id.v1")) / IOutboxWriter ✅ 21 Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ RabbitMQ broker 适配 + 消费者 + DLQ 下游服务间事件总线的默认 broker AddKunEventsBroker / AddKunEventsSubscriber ✅ — Kun.Saga Saga Orchestration（步骤 / 反向补偿 / 超时 / 实例持久化） 跨服务长事务（下单-支付-发货） AddKunSaga() / ISagaStep ⚠️ trim-safe 18 Kun.Saga 已归档（S1-KUN-025）：移出解决方案，包名停发，没有替代的包；Order 样例改成不带编排的命令流程。上表与下面非 AOT 白名单里的这一行按原样保留。 宿主与通信（Host 层） 模块 职责 典型用途 主要 API AOT 测试 Kun.AspNetCore Minimal API 命令和查询端点映射 下游服务的对外 HTTP 路由 MapCommand / MapQuery ⚠️ trim-safe 5 Kun.Grpc gRPC 跟踪、服务认证、租户边界、权限装配检查与结果映射 服务间内部 RPC；Catalog / Order gRPC endpoint AddKunGrpc() / KunResultToRpcInterceptor ✅ 7 Kun.Gateway.Abstractions 网关服务端口、配置与静态路由契约 宿主与平台组件共享 GatewayConfiguration ✅ — Kun.Gateway YARP + 外部 JWT 校验 + S2S JWT 签发 + JWKS endpoint + 限流 统一边界：外部 JWT 验证 + 内部 S2S JWT 签发 AddKunGateway() / MapKunJwks() ✅ 21 Kun.Gateway.Shell 外壳静态托管、引导端点与组件登记 平台网关宿主 AddKunGatewayShell() ✅ — 安全、多租户、审计 title: Kun 版本记录
content:
本页适用 v2026.11.24。
本页镜像自正式发布段所在提交的 CHANGELOG.md（v2026.11.24）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；平台集成方式见内核与平台组件。

[2026.11.24] - 2026-11-24

Changed — 端点权限回调的校验

MapKunData、MapKunDataTypes、MapKunDataConnections 与 MapKunFiles 的权限回调须给端点加上执行同一权限点的授权要求，RequireKunPermission 即如此。构造端点时核对三项：端点带该权限点的 RequiresPermissionAttribute；授权策略里有权限点相同的 Kun.Authorization.IPermissionEnforcementRequirement；端点没有匿名放行标记，外层分组上的也算。任一项不满足即抛出 InvalidOperationException。按名字引用的策略在构造端点时看不到其中的要求，不算接上。自定义执行点让自己的授权要求实现 IPermissionEnforcementRequirement。

Added — 权限执行要求的标记接口

内核契约 Kun.Authorization 新增 IPermissionEnforcementRequirement，由执行权限点的授权要求实现。RequireKunPermission 加上的要求已实现它。

Changed — gRPC 权限点在启动时校验

登记了 AddKunAuthorization 的宿主在启动时核对 gRPC 方法上 RequiresPermissionAttribute 的权限点。不是 <plugin-id>:<resource>:<action> 全名的，宿主启动即抛出 InvalidOperationException，消息列出方法与权限点。

补充 2026.11.21 一节「HTTP 和 gRPC 授权执行点」：其中「在端点声明时抛出」只适用于 HTTP 的 RequireKunPermission。在该版里，gRPC 方法上不是全名的权限点要到调用时才被拒绝。

Changed — 授权包的来源

补充 2026.11.21 一节「HTTP 和 gRPC 授权执行点」：Kun.Authorization.AspNetCore 属于平台档，从 CavaiLAB 的 GitHub Packages 还原。原来用 Kun.AspNetCore 的 RequireKunPermission，或在 Kun.Grpc 的服务方法上标 [RequiresPermission] 的项目，升级后要引用这个包；只从 nuget.org 还原的项目要为它映射 GitHub Packages 的源。没有登记授权拦截器时，Kun.Grpc 拒绝执行标了 [RequiresPermission] 的方法。

Changed — 异常信息

以下异常的消息文字有调整，异常类型、错误码与触发条件不变：KunDataMisconfiguredException 的四条装配错误（迁移生成器、软删除拦截器、数据模型约定、模型约定只用于 KunStrictDbContext），以及 AddKunCapability 在框架当前主体端口解析为匿名兜底时的启动检查（InvalidOperationException）。按消息原文匹配的代码请改为按异常类型或错误码判断。

Fixed — 按配置绑定租户连接串（S1-KUN-024）

Database 隔离策略用 Configure<TenantsConnectionOptions>(configuration.GetSection(TenantsConnectionOptions.SectionName)) 绑定的连接串现在会生效。配置绑定器不支持以 Guid 为键的字典，2026.11.21 中这一节的配置进不了 ConnectionStrings，按租户解析连接串时报未配置。TenantsConnectionOptions 新增 ConfiguredConnectionStrings，承接配置里的 ConnectionStrings 节；AddKunMultiTenancy<TContext> 选 TenantIsolation.Database 时，宿主启动阶段校验每个键并把它们并入 ConnectionStrings。配置的写法不变。

键须是非空 UUID 的小写 D 格式。键不合法，或同一租户在代码与配置里的连接串不一致时，宿主启动失败，错误信息里写出那个键。开启配置绑定源生成器的项目，生成的代码按 Guid.Parse 解析键：大写、带花括号的键原先能绑定，现在启动即失败；完全不是 UUID 的键在绑定时由生成的代码报错。

Fixed — 文件组件的版本

Fixed — 补记 2026.11.21 事件与审计的行为变化与删除项

2026.11.21 的事件与审计各节没有写全的行为变化与删除项，补记如下：

自 2026.11.21 起，普通事件经 RabbitMQ 发布时不要求路由到队列（mandatory: false）：没有队列绑定该事件的路由键时，broker 丢弃这条事件并照常确认，Outbox 行标为已发布。此前 Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ 的发布器按 mandatory 发布，路由不到时发布报错、由 Outbox 重试；现在不报错也不重试。需要接收事件的宿主要先部署订阅、让队列完成绑定，再让生产方发送。

自 2026.11.21 起，实体审计的保存需要主体：不在 EventEnvelopeScope 内（命令管道会打开它）、AuditContext.ActorId 为空、当前用户也未认证时，拦截器拒绝这次保存，抛出错误码为 EVENTS_PUBLISH_REJECTED 的 KunEventsException，业务实体、审计日志与 Outbox 都不写入。后台作业、匿名请求等没有已认证用户的保存，要先用 EventEnvelopeScope.Begin 以实际的服务主体打开作用域，打开后可用同一上下文重试。

2026.11.21 的两节 Fixed（RabbitMQ 连接已被对端关掉时的释放、订阅端停止时的确认）写的是 RabbitMqConnectionProvider 与当时的订阅端，这两样在同一版里已经删除，2026.11.21 的包里没有。现在的订阅端（由 AddKunEventsSubscriber 登记）停止时同样不在正在关的通道上确认或拒绝，关通道遇到连接已被对端关掉时照常释放通道。

2026.11.21 还删除了下列公共类型，前文没有逐个列出：
Kun.EventBus：Kun.EventBus.Background 下除 IOutboxLockProvider、RedisOutboxLockProvider 以外的类型，即 IOutboxMessageStore、IOutboxBatchStore、NullOutboxLockProvider、OutboxPublisherOptions 与前文列过的 OutboxPublisherBackgroundService；以及 Kun.EventBus.DependencyInjection.KunOutboxPublisherExtensions。

Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ：此前的公共类型全部删除，即 RabbitMqConnectionProvider、Options.RabbitMqOptions、Publishing.RabbitMqIntegrationEventPublisher、Consuming.RabbitMqIntegrationEventSubscriber、DependencyInjection.KunRabbitMqBuilder 与 DependencyInjection.KunRabbitMqServiceCollectionExtensions（命名空间都在 Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ 下）。现在的公共类型是 KunEventsRabbitMqExtensions、KunEventsSubscriberBuilder 与 KunEventsSubscriberOptions。

Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore：AuditSaveChangesInterceptor、EfAuditWriter<TDbContext>、PostgresAuditChain 与 DependencyInjection.KunAuditEntityFrameworkCoreServiceCollectionExtensions（AddKunAuditEntityFrameworkCore、UseEntityFramework<TDbContext>、UsePostgresChain），命名空间都在 Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore 下。替代用法见前文「命令链与实体审计」。
